A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TS-SNN research. Their text, equations, tables, seven figures, and Appendix A.1–A.5 are readable and support reliable comparison despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification experiments, component ablations, computational-energy estimates, and the appendix firing-rate comparison.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results, including classification outcomes in Tables 1–4 and firing-rate measurements in Appendix A.5.

M1.justification: The temporal channel shifts, random split points, zero-padding and truncation, and residual combination with alpha remain unchanged in Section 3 and Algorithm 1. The added single-timestep explanation introduces no new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same static-image classification tasks on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and ImageNet, and event-based classification on CIFAR10-DVS. No dataset, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in Tables 1–4 and the appendix firing-rate comparison. The changed citation suffixes for MPBN and RMP-Loss refer to the same methods.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix A.2–A.3 retain the same splits, augmentations, architectures, timesteps, batch sizes, and training schedules. No new evaluation protocol is reported.

E4.justification: The channel-folding, shift-strategy, shift-direction, and training-versus-inference ablations are retained unchanged, as are the computational-efficiency and firing-rate analyses. The new single-timestep discussion adds no experiment testing its explanation.

E5.justification: Both versions describe Table 1 accuracy as the mean and standard deviation of three trials and retain the same uncertainty reporting elsewhere. No seed information, additional run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: The numerical tables, plotted results, and reported experimental findings are unchanged. Examples include 96.72% on CIFAR-10, 80.28% on CIFAR-100, 70.61% on ImageNet, and appendix firing rates of 33.06% for vanilla SNN versus 35.61% for TS-SNN.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(10), the neuron definitions, temporal-shift formulation, and energy-estimation assumptions remain unchanged. The added single-timestep paragraph provides a qualitative interpretation without a new formal derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about lightweight temporal fusion, residual feature preservation, accuracy with fewer timesteps, architectural compatibility, and energy efficiency.

C2.justification: v1 already discusses limited temporal modeling at T=1. Section 4.3 in v5 adds that performance gains in this setting may arise from the existing alpha scaling mechanism, providing a new tentative explanation without experimental confirmation.

D1.justification: The PyTorch implementation, GPU hardware, optimizer, hyperparameters, preprocessing, and alpha initialization details are retained in Section 4.1 and Appendix A.2–A.4. No new code or data access information is provided.

R1.justification: Section 2.2 adds references to STAA-SNN and FSTA-SNN, including a brief description of frequency-based spatiotemporal modeling. The existing TSM motivation and overall novelty positioning remain unchanged; bibliographic year and suffix updates do not represent additional works.

P1.justification: Changes comprise the short single-timestep explanation, limited related-work additions, correspondence and funding updates, and bibliographic edits. The section organization and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Tables 2 and 3 gain explicit dataset header rows, and equation spacing, bibliography typography, and page flow change. All seven figures retain the same visual content; no figure or table is added or removed.

improvement.justification: The added Section 4.3 discussion usefully distinguishes temporal mixing from the possible contribution of alpha at T=1, making the existing results easier to interpret. The two related-work additions modestly improve context. These gains are limited because the mechanism explanation remains untested and the empirical evidence and reproducibility information are unchanged.
